primary_sources.title: TSMC 3Q26 earnings call transcript
facts: 7nm and below contributed 79% of wafer revenue
3Q gross margin declined 130bp sequentially primarily from initial 2nm ramp
4Q midpoint gross-margin decline is attributed to continued 2nm ramp and overseas-fab dilution, partly offset by productivity and across-node capacity optimization
management described AI accelerator demand as extremely robust and saw no slowdown

causal_thesis: TSMC's rapid N2 ramp creates a measurable near-term margin headwind while simultaneously deepening leading-edge mix. If yield learning, productivity and across-node capacity optimization offset N2 start-up and overseas-fab dilution, normalized earnings power can expand without requiring perpetual gross-margin peaks. This mechanism is foundry process-economics, not equipment scarcity.
active_disconfirmation: The observed 66.4% margin is already below 2Q26 because N2 ramp diluted margin; ramp economics can worsen or last longer than expected.
Overseas fabs structurally dilute margin and may offset scale/productivity gains.
AI-demand statements are forward-looking and customer capex can slow, double-order or shift architectures.
Advanced-node mix does not guarantee incremental returns if depreciation, labor, utility or packaging costs rise faster than pricing/productivity.
Geopolitical concentration and overseas expansion can impose costs not captured by current quarter margins.
A correct operating thesis does not imply an attractive security valuation.
